transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Could you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi… thanks. I guess the main thing is I’ve been having trouble staying on track. It’s not like I’m trying to avoid things, but I get pulled away really easily—like one Slack notification, or even a song lyric or a random idea for another project, and then I’ve completely lost the thread of what I was doing. Like, I’ll be working on a dashboard I’m supposed to finish, and suddenly I’m somewhere else mentally. I don’t know if that makes sense or if it’s serious enough to bring in, but it’s been frustrating.
Can you tell me if you often forget things, have trouble keeping track of tasks, or find yourself easily distracted even when you’re trying to focus?

Yeah… I think easily distracted is probably the biggest one. I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, but I get pulled off track really fast. Like one Slack ping, or even a song lyric popping into my head, or some random idea for another project, and then I realize I’ve completely lost where I was in the dashboard I was supposed to be finishing. It’s not that I’m not trying—I am—but my attention just kind of… slips. Does that answer what you mean?
Do these distractions and difficulties staying focused happen in other areas of your life, like at home, in conversations, or in social situations, or is it mainly at work?

I think it’s mostly noticeable with work or school-type tasks, if that makes sense. Like when I’m supposed to be finishing a dashboard, one Slack ping or even just a song lyric in my head can pull me away, and then I’ve lost the thread. I’m not sure I’ve paid as much attention to it in social situations… but the staying-focused part is definitely why I came in.
Do you also find yourself getting distracted or losing focus during tasks at home, like when doing chores, reading, or watching something?

Yeah, I guess it does happen at home too, though I maybe notice it less. Like if I sit down to read a research article or watch a UX tutorial, I’ll think I’m following it, but then after a few minutes I realize my eyes have been moving across the page or the screen and I have no idea what I just took in. It’s kind of embarrassing, because I’m technically “doing” the thing, but not really absorbing it. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Looking back, were you also someone who had trouble focusing or got distracted easily when you were younger, like in school or while doing homework?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I did okay in school overall, so I don’t want to make it sound like I was constantly in trouble or anything. But even in elementary school, I remember teachers writing little comments about me rushing through worksheets or missing directions because I’d kind of lose track of what I was supposed to be doing.

And with homework, my parents would sit next to me sometimes, not because I couldn’t understand it, but because I’d wander off or start doing something else before I finished. I also apparently talked over people in group work, which is… not my favorite thing to admit. But yes, looking back, it was probably there earlier too. Does that help?
